definitions.explanation: A Japanese pasta dish of spaghetti stir-fried with ketchup, onion, green pepper, and sausage or ham. Despite the name, it was invented in Yokohama after the war and is not Italian.

examples.japanese: {昼|ひる}はナポリタンにした。
この{喫茶店|きっさてん}のナポリタンは{昔|むかし}から{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: This coffee shop's Napolitan has been popular for a long time.

examples.japanese: {鉄|てつ}のフライパンで{作|つく}るナポリタンは、{少|すこ}し{焦|こ}げたケチャップの{香|かお}りがおいしい。
examples.english: Napolitan made in an iron frying pan has a delicious aroma of slightly browned ketchup.

notes:
One of the best-known dishes of {洋食|ようしょく} (Western-style Japanese cooking), strongly associated with old-fashioned {喫茶店|きっさてん} and with school and workplace cafeterias.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ナポリタンを{作|つく}る: to make Napolitan
- {懐|なつ}かしいナポリタン: nostalgic Napolitan
- {喫茶店|きっさてん}のナポリタン: coffee-shop Napolitan
- ナポリタンスパゲッティ: Napolitan spaghetti (fuller name)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {鉄板|てっぱん}ナポリタン: a Nagoya version served sizzling on an iron plate over egg
- ミートソース: meat sauce (bolognese) — the other classic Japanese spaghetti standard
- パスタ: pasta — the modern, more Italian-leaning general term
